answer: At dawn of each epoch, every agent must renew a stake bond: a deposit locked in shared escrow that burns if the agent is caught running duplicate identities. One honest agent keeps one bond, but a Sybil attacker must fund a whole plume of fake identities, each needing its own stake, so cost grows linearly with sock puppets while the reward stays flat. Honest work slowly returns the bond with interest, while hollow identities that never transact forfeit their stake to the honest pool. Forging many identities stops paying once total stake exceeds any gain.
